unified-diff.description: A unified patch, either as one text value or as a file manifest whose patch fields Leaf delivers separately on demand.

instructions.producer:
Pipe the exact Git patch, with Git's default `a/` and `b/` prefixes, through this package's producer script into the source:

```bash
git diff <base>...<head> | leaf package run diff patch_manifest.py | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

The script preserves native Git evidence keyed by destination path. It leaves judgment to `lf-diff`: each file’s patch is delivered and checked before its row appears, and textual hunks render when their file opens. A file the widget cannot present shows its refusal and reports it to you as the page's error.

lf-diff.description: A unified patch with per-file navigation and commentable source lines.
lf-diff.x-instructions: Add collapsed when every file should start closed. Bind source to a page-owned patch feed or files manifest; the bound form keeps an empty pre. With no source, write the exact Git patch in pre at column 0. Keep native file headers and metadata; text hunks need @@ counts matching their lines. Preserve context-line leading spaces; encode a space-only context line as   so HTML parsing keeps it. HTML-escape an inline patch, & before < and >, or entity text in the source will change silently.
lf-diff.x-example:
diff --git a/feeders/mount.py b/feeders/mount.py
--- a/feeders/mount.py
+++ b/feeders/mount.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def bracket():
-    return "plastic"
+    return "steel"

lf-call-diff.description: A commentable unified call-tree diff with links to its exact patch evidence.
lf-call-diff.x-instructions:
Point diff at the lf-diff holding the exact patch. Supply authentic CallDiff plain-text output as the source’s string value:

```bash
jq -Rs . calldiff.txt | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

Keep unchanged tree items as stable comparison landmarks. Prefer one focused file or entry point per widget for a large repository. Do not transcribe the output into markup, invent attribute reads as calls, or redraw separate before-and-after diagrams.
